abstract: UHD-1/4K and UHD-2/8K satellite broadcasts were launched on 1 December 2018 in Japan. One of these services, the broadcast of UHD-2/8K was the first of its kind in the world. This broadcasting system adopts high-efficiency video coding (HEVC) with highly efficient compression performance, a newly developed (Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting) ISDB-S3 transmission system, which uses the 16APSK modulation scheme and other new technologies. In this paper, we provide details of the new UHD-1/4K and UHD-2/8K services, focusing on standardizing technical specifications and practical ways to introduce new reception systems into households.

authors.bio: Katsuya Hayashi received an associate degree in information technology from the Tsuyama College, National Institute of Technology, Tsuyama, Japan, and joined Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Tokyo, Japan, in 2000. He was initially engaged in the management of digital broadcasting transmission and reception systems at Tottori, Yamaguchi, and Hiroshima branch broadcasting stations. Since 2017, he has been involved in standardizing the digital broadcasting reception system with the Transmission and Reception Engineering Center, NHK.
authors.name: Katsuya Hayashi

authors.bio: Kazuhiro Kumamaru received a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from the Tokyo University of Science, Tokyo, Japan, in 2007, the master’s degree in electrical and electronic engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, and joined NHK in 2009. He was engaged in implementing digital broadcasting stations at Hiroshima branch stations from 2009 to 2014. He was engaged in the designing and installation of studio to transmitter link/transmitter to transmitter link (STL/TTL) equipment at the Transmission and Reception Engineering Center from 2014 to 2017. Since 2017, he has been involved in standardizing broadcasting satellite and has been participating in International Telecommunication Union– Radiocommunication (ITU-R) meetings.
authors.name: Kazuhiro Kumamaru

authors.bio: Shinsuke Yokozawa received BE and ME degrees in communication engineering and informatics from the University of Electro-Communications, Tokyo, Japan, in 2010 and 2012, respectively. He joined NHK in 2012, and has been working with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories since 2015. He is a researcher at the Advanced Transmission Systems Research Division, where his interests include next-generation satellite broadcasting systems. He received the Young Researcher’s Award of Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers (IEICE) in 2020. He is a member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), IEICE, and the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers (ITE).
authors.name: Shinsuke Yokozawa
